questions.question_text:
Solve $\dfrac{\sin\theta}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 35^{\circ}}{6}$ for $\theta$, given that $\theta$ is obtuse.
Answer to $1$ decimal place.

options.why: Gave the acute value from $\sin^{-1}$, but the stem says the angle is obtuse.
Divided the wrong way, using $6\sin 35^{\circ}/10$, then took the supplement.

questions.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{10}=\dfrac{\sin 35^{\circ}}{6}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{10\sin 35^{\circ}}{6}$
The inverse sine gives the acute angle $72.9020\ldots^{\circ}$. Since $\theta$ is obtuse:
$\theta=180^{\circ}-72.9020\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 107.1^{\circ}$

options.why: Took the supplement $180^{\circ}-47.9^{\circ}$ although $\theta$ is acute.

questions.solution_text:
$\theta$ is opposite the $8$ cm side, and the $68^{\circ}$ angle is opposite the $10$ cm side.
$\dfrac{\sin\theta}{8}=\dfrac{\sin 68^{\circ}}{10}$
$\sin\theta=\dfrac{8\sin 68^{\circ}}{10}$
$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{8\sin 68^{\circ}}{10}\right)$
$=47.8898\ldots^{\circ}$
$\approx 47.9^{\circ}$
